localLife.nature: Flat valley floor, full sun, almost no shade canopy — the kind of heat that radiates off asphalt and parking lots long after sundown.
localLife.community: Aerospace and warehouse crews around the airport, small shops and restaurants along Victory and Van Nuys Boulevard, multigenerational households in duplexes and post-war single-family blocks.
localLife.howWeHelp: When it's 105 for the fifth day straight, we're the reason the corner restaurant kitchen stays open and the family in the 1958 duplex isn't sleeping in the living room.

seasonalNotes.focus: Peak season — the heat island effect means Van Nuys often runs hotter than the coast by 15+ degrees, and older ducting can't keep up without a tune-up first.
Mild, but older heaters that sat unused all summer need a check before the first cold snap.
